domain_title: Human impact, rights, fairness, transparency, oversight and recourse
title: Meaningful human oversight
canonical_definition: Competent humans have sufficient information, authority, time and technical ability to review, intervene, override and escalate at material decision points.

conditions: When human oversight is claimed, required or relied upon as a control.
Record the assessed release, operating scope and evidence that supports any applicability decision.

primary_questions.question: Are oversight purpose, reviewer competence, information needs, intervention points and authority defined?
Can reviewers actually inspect evidence, pause, correct, override and escalate without undue friction or incentive bias?
Do intervention, disagreement, error and workload data demonstrate that oversight is effective rather than nominal?

capability_indicators: Effectiveness and automation bias are monitored

conditions: Refer a material failure of meaningful human oversight to the accountable authority before a consequential transition.

normative_source_mappings.relevant_locator: NIST AI 100-1, GOVERN 3.2 (PDF p. 28), MAP 3.5 (PDF p. 32), MEASURE 4.3 (PDF p. 36)
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: The voluntary framework provides guidance on defining human oversight responsibilities, assessing oversight, and tracking outcomes. The SAE criteria define the object-specific rules. Confirm any binding obligation through the accountable authority and its applicable source.

governance_purpose: Make meaningful human oversight verifiable against the current AI system, decision context and accountable ownership.
distinct_claim: E4 evaluates meaningful human oversight using evidence from intent through operation. AP-E4 independently assesses evidence of rubber-stamp oversight.

atomic_subcriteria.criterion: The versioned definition identifies an oversight specification naming competent reviewers, information needs, intervention points, workload and decision authority. Record the accountable owner, scope and material assumptions.

The current release demonstrates operative review, pause, correction, override and escalation paths with access to relevant evidence and recorded disagreement. Trace the decisions and controls to attributable records.

Representative, executed evidence provides observed workload, intervention and disagreement records plus exercises showing reviewers can detect and correct errors. Compare expected and observed outcomes and record exceptions.
For an operating system, current records cover the material paths involved in meaningful human oversight, including relevant exceptions and changes.

required_evidence.title: Versioned scope and control definition
required_evidence.description: Provide an oversight specification naming competent reviewers, information needs, intervention points, workload and decision authority. Include the affected workflow, current version and accountable owner.

required_evidence.title: Effective implementation records
required_evidence.description: Demonstrate operative review, pause, correction, override and escalation paths with access to relevant evidence and recorded disagreement. Trace the scope, control and authority to the current implementation, including exceptions.

required_evidence.title: Representative verification results
required_evidence.description: Provide observed workload, intervention and disagreement records plus exercises showing reviewers can detect and correct errors. Include current version, test scope, criteria, expected and observed outcomes, and unresolved failures.

required_evidence.title: Current operating or change evidence
required_evidence.description: Retain dated records that show how meaningful human oversight works for the assessed scope, including the relevant exceptions and any material change since the evidence was captured.

sufficiency: Start with an oversight specification naming competent reviewers, information needs, intervention points, workload and decision authority. Reconcile it against the effective controls and representative results for the same operating scope and version.

Use observed workload, intervention and disagreement records plus exercises showing reviewers can detect and correct errors to support effectiveness at the relevant lifecycle stage. Record missing paths and unresolved conflicts as UNKNOWN. A verified shortfall can support a gap without resolving the other questions.
Reassess affected evidence after a material change. An accountable human validates or approves the result where required by the lifecycle target.
evidence_rules.evidence_ceiling: A specification supports DECLARED intent. Effective implementation records may support IMPLEMENTED. Representative executed tests support TESTED within their scope. Current operating evidence supports OPERATIONALLY_OBSERVED for covered paths and time. Record human assurance independently.
false_positive_guards: Low override rates require context about error prevalence and reviewer capability before drawing a conclusion.
Reconcile document claims with the effective release, actual operation and relevant exceptions before recording satisfaction.
prohibited_inferences: A capability gap alone cannot establish AP-E4 presence.
An approved design or evidence plan cannot establish test execution or operational effectiveness.
Satisfying this capability cannot by itself authorize progression or establish legal compliance.

finding_definitions.title: Material definition or intent gap in meaningful human oversight
Verified implementation or effectiveness gap in meaningful human oversight
Evidence remains insufficient for meaningful human oversight in the assessed scope
